title: A2A HTTP Transport DNS-Rebinding TOCTOU Hardening

threat_model.description: Attacker controls authoritative DNS for their domain with TTL=0. Returns a public IP at validation time (passes blocklist check), then flips the record to a private IP by connect time. The urllib OS resolver calls getaddrinfo again at TCP connect, receiving the private IP and establishing a connection to the internal target.
threat_model.prerequisite: Attacker controls an authoritative DNS server for a domain they own
threat_model.window: Milliseconds between _validate_url DNS call and urllib OS resolver call at connect()

mitigation.mechanism: Resolve hostname once via _resolve_and_pin_host, validate the IP, then build a custom urllib opener (_PinnedHTTPHandler / _PinnedHTTPSHandler) whose do_open creates http.client.HTTPConnection/HTTPSConnection targeting the pinned IP. OS resolver is never called again for that hop.
mitigation.host_header: Injected as original hostname so virtual-hosting and CDN routing work correctly
mitigation.tls_sni: _PinnedHTTPSConnection.connect() passes server_hostname=original_host to ssl.wrap_socket so TLS SNI and certificate validation use the correct name
mitigation.redirect_handling: Every redirect hop independently re-resolves and re-pins the Location hostname; pinned IP from hop N never reused for hop N+1
mitigation.escape_hatch: allow_private_networks=True or AUTODEV_A2A_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS env var bypasses IP-pinning for integration tests

tests.name: test_dns_rebinding_connect_to_pinned_public_ip
tests.scenario: DNS returns public IP at validate time; hypothetical third call would return private IP; pinned connection uses public IP only

tests.name: test_different_public_ip_at_connect_time_succeeds
tests.scenario: Two different public IPs at validate vs. pin time; both safe; request succeeds

tests.name: test_redirect_to_public_hostname_allowed

tests.name: test_max_redirects_5_enforced

tests.name: test_ipv6_redirect_to_loopback_rejected

tests.name: test_resolve_and_pin_host_returns_public_ip

residual_risks.title: Egress-proxy SSRF
residual_risks.description: Attacker controls a public proxy that internally forwards requests to private hosts. The proxy's public IP passes all IP-range checks; the tunneling is invisible to this adapter.
residual_risks.mitigation_available: Network-egress firewall or transparent proxy enforcing IP-range restrictions at kernel/routing layer

residual_risks.title: Kernel-level network attacks
residual_risks.description: Routing table manipulation, anycast hijacking, on-path BGP interception after connect() returns. Pure-Python code has no visibility into these.
residual_risks.mitigation_available: RPKI, BGPsec, mutual TLS, certificate pinning at PKI level
